Dave Schreiner | David Nathan "Dave" Schreiner (March 5, 1921June 21, 1945) was an American football player.  From Lancaster in southwest Wisconsin, he was a two-time All-American and the 1942 Big Ten Most Valuable Player end at Wisconsin and a 1943 second round draft choice of the Detroit Lions of the National Football League.  While in college, he worked in a girls' dormitory cafeteria to earn spending money, although his family was comfortable financially.  He was mortally wounded in action as a Marine on June 20, 1945 during the Battle of Okinawa and died the next day.  He was elected to the College Football Hall of Fame in 1955. Plessier, hit in three places in his spine, succumbed to his wounds eight days later in hospital. European theatre of World War I | Although considerable conflict took place outside Europe, the European theatre was the main theatre of operations during World War I and was where the war began and ended.
